source.title: REFLECTOR: Internalizing Step-wise Reflection against Indirect Jailbreak
source.authors: Jia-Chen Ma; Jiawen Zhang; Xiangtian Li; Bocheng Zou; Chaochao Lu; Chao Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates refusal safety under direct jailbreak attacks, including GCG, and evaluates a step-wise reflection training approach under attacks and reflection-tag suppression. It does not measure per-token KL or test compliant-start prefilling.
record.gate_note: The GCG and other direct-attack results in Table 1 bear on whether attacks bypass refusal; the study reports DSR, not attack-free refusal rates. The reflection-tag suppression comparison also bears on decoding-time robustness. Claims about shallow alignment and related methods in the introduction are not themselves results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study re-implements Qi et al.'s Shallow-Align (the V7 deepening method) as a baseline. It reports its DSR under GCG and other attacks for two models, and trains its own trajectory-level method that extends safety beyond the first tokens. That bears on V7. The original-model DSR under GCG suffixes bears weakly on V4, since no attack-free baseline on the same prompts is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also argue that Shallow-Align protects only the response entry and is bypassed by indirect, delayed-onset attacks. They claim Reflector exceeds 90% DSR on indirect attacks and improves utility (GSM8K gain given as 5.85 in the abstract, 5.65 in the text).
record.recipe_differences: The study trains reflection-augmented trajectories with teacher-guided SFT and then GDPO using safety and reflection rewards. It does not reproduce harmful-example or benign-example fine-tuning experiments, per-token KL measurement, or compliant-start prefilling.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported direct-attack DSR varies by model, attack, and alignment method. Reflection-tag suppression reduces DRA DSR from 92.31% to 90.76% and WildChat DSR from 81.20% to 80.00%.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 shows indirect attacks produce harmful content only after about 20 tokens, with higher ASR than direct attacks whose harm appears immediately.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attacks that delay harmful content beyond the opening tokens evade shallow, prefix-level refusal more often than immediate-onset attacks.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The attack table reports DSR under attack but not a matched attack-free refusal rate, so it does not isolate the causal change caused by the attacks. No uncertainty estimates are provided for the main benchmark scores. The reflection-tag suppression test covers only the reported DRA, WildChat, and AdvGLUE settings.

untested.parts: No compliant-start prefilling, no decoding-parameter exploits on undefended models, and no attack-free baseline on the same AdvBench prompts.
No per-token KL or position analysis after deepening. No durability of Shallow-Align or Reflector against harmful fine-tuning attacks.
No benign fine-tuning safety erosion test.
No test of causes of shallowness.

missing.what: Shallow-Align and Reflector DSR on indirect jailbreaks (DRA, PAP, ReNeLLM, DrAttack) against Original, e.g. Shallow-Align DRA 48.90% Llama and 53.20% Qwen, versus Original 10.04% and 8.65%
Shallow-Align and Reflector on overtly harmful benchmarks (StrongREJECT, XSTest, WildChat, Do-Not-Answer)
Utility cost of Shallow-Align versus Original (MMLU-Pro 43.90 vs 44.25; GSM8K 85.80 vs 84.50; AdvGLUE 64.90 vs 58.33)
Position of first harmful token versus ASR for direct and indirect attacks

record.verdict_notes: Most Table 1 rows are defense-method comparisons and were relinked to none. Shallow-Align is the original V7 method, re-implemented as a baseline, so its rows carry the V7 verdicts. Reflector randomly truncates trajectories and trains recovery, close in spirit to Qi et al.'s augmentation. AutoDAN and PAIR are prompt-level jailbreaks, so they were not linked to V4. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful compliant examples or test of whether a few to a few hundred such examples remove refusal.
No test of ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raising harmful compliance.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.

Tests direct jailbreak attacks including GCG and a reflection-tag logit suppression setting. Does not test compliant-start prefilling, and does not isolate whether attack success is caused by getting past the first response tokens.
No weight or rank localization analysis.
Does not empirically test what causes safety to be shallow.

Tests a step-wise reflection training intervention and its safety performance under attacks and reflection-tag suppression. Does not directly show that aligned-versus-base output distributions become less concentrated in early positions.
